pt.title: Energia Impulsiona a Inflação: Por Dentro do Salto de 0,4% nos Preços ao Consumidor em Outubro

segments.src: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, a faster pace than most forecasters expected, while core inflation, which leaves out food and energy, held at 0.3%.
segments.tr: Os preços ao consumidor subiram 0,4% em outubro, um ritmo mais rápido do que a maioria dos analistas esperava, enquanto o núcleo da inflação, que exclui alimentos e energia, manteve-se em 0,3%.

segments.src: The gap between those two numbers points to the main driver of the month: energy.
segments.tr: A lacuna entre esses dois números aponta para o principal impulsionador do mês: a energia.

segments.src: This article explains what the headline and core figures mean, which categories fed the increase, and why one strong monthly reading doesn't settle the debate over where inflation is heading.
segments.tr: Este artigo explica o que significam os dados cheios e o núcleo, quais categorias alimentaram o aumento e por que uma leitura mensal forte não resolve o debate sobre para onde a inflação está indo.

segments.src: ## The Numbers at a Glance
segments.tr: ## Os Números em Destaque

segments.src: - **Headline consumer prices:** up 0.4% for the month, above forecasts.
segments.tr: - **Preços ao consumidor cheios:** alta de 0,4% no mês, acima das previsões.

segments.src: - **Core prices (excluding food and energy):** up 0.3%, unchanged from the prior pace.
segments.tr: - **Preços do núcleo (excluindo alimentos e energia):** alta de 0,3%, inalterados em relação ao ritmo anterior.

segments.src: - **The difference:** roughly 0.1 percentage point, which is attributable mostly to more volatile categories such as energy.
segments.tr: - **A diferença:** aproximadamente 0,1 ponto percentual, atribuível principalmente a categorias mais voláteis, como a energia.

segments.src: A 0.4% monthly gain looks modest, but economists often look at what it implies over a year.
segments.tr: Um ganho mensal de 0,4% parece modesto, mas os economistas costumam observar o que ele implica ao longo de um ano.

segments.src: If a 0.4% pace held for twelve months, it would compound to close to 5% annual inflation.
segments.tr: Se o ritmo de 0,4% se mantivesse por doze meses, acumularia uma inflação anual próxima de 5%.

segments.src: That is well above the 2% target the Federal Reserve has set.
segments.tr: Isso está bem acima da meta de 2% definida pelo Federal Reserve.

segments.src: A 0.3% pace compounds to a little under 4%.
segments.tr: Um ritmo de 0,3% acumula um pouco abaixo de 4%.

segments.src: That is why even small monthly differences get close attention.
segments.tr: É por isso que até mesmo pequenas diferenças mensais recebem atenção cuidadosa.

segments.src: ## Why Energy Mattered So Much
segments.tr: ## Por Que a Energia Importou Tanto

segments.src: Energy prices are among the most volatile parts of the consumer price index.
segments.tr: Os preços da energia estão entre as partes mais voláteis do índice de preços ao consumidor.

segments.src: Gasoline, electricity, and natural gas can all move sharply from month to month because of weather, refinery activity, seasonal demand, and global supply conditions.
segments.tr: Gasolina, eletricidade e gás natural podem variar bruscamente de mês para mês devido ao clima, à atividade das refinarias, à demanda sazonal e às condições globais de oferta.

segments.src: Energy has an outsized effect on headline readings for three reasons:
segments.tr: A energia tem um efeito desproporcional nas leituras cheias por três razões:

segments.src: 1. **It is bought often.** Households fill up their tanks and pay utility bills every month, so changes are felt quickly.
segments.tr: 1. **É comprada com frequência.** As famílias abastecem os seus tanques e pagam as contas de serviços públicos todos os meses, portanto as mudanças são sentidas rapidamente.

segments.src: 2. **It is volatile.** A swing of several percent in a single month is not unusual, which can move the overall index even when other prices are steady.
segments.tr: 2. **É volátil.** Uma oscilação de vários por cento num único mês não é incomum, o que pode mover o índice geral mesmo quando outros preços estão estáveis.

segments.src: 3. **It feeds into other costs.** Higher fuel and power costs can eventually show up in transportation, shipping, and food prices.
segments.tr: 3. **Alimenta outros custos.** Custos mais altos de combustível e energia podem eventualmente refletir no transporte, no frete e nos preços dos alimentos.

segments.src: Because the headline index includes energy and the core index does not, an energy-led month tends to lift the first number while leaving the second largely unchanged.
segments.tr: Como o índice cheio inclui energia e o núcleo não inclui, um mês impulsionado pela energia tende a elevar o primeiro número, deixando o segundo praticamente inalterado.

segments.src: That is the pattern seen in October.
segments.tr: Esse foi o padrão visto em outubro.

segments.src: ## Other Categories in the Mix
segments.tr: ## Outras Categorias no Conjunto

segments.src: Energy was not the only contributor.
segments.tr: A energia não foi a única contribuição.

segments.src: Several other areas typically shape the monthly reading:
segments.tr: Várias outras áreas costumam moldar a leitura mensal:

segments.src: - **Shelter.** Rent and housing-related costs make up the largest single share of the index. They move slowly, but they rarely fall quickly, so they often hold core inflation up.
segments.tr: - **Habitação.** Aluguéis e custos relacionados à moradia representam a maior parcela individual do índice. Eles se movem devagar, mas raramente caem rápido, por isso costumam sustentar o núcleo da inflação.

segments.src: - **Food.** Grocery and restaurant prices can add or subtract a few hundredths of a percentage point depending on the month.
segments.tr: - **Alimentos.** Os preços nos supermercados e restaurantes podem somar ou subtrair alguns centésimos de ponto percentual, dependendo do mês.

segments.src: - **Services.** Items such as medical care, insurance, and transportation services have been persistent sources of upward pressure in recent years.
segments.tr: - **Serviços.** Itens como cuidados médicos, seguros e serviços de transporte têm sido fontes persistentes de pressão de alta nos últimos anos.

segments.src: - **Goods.** Prices for many manufactured goods have been flatter, which helps offset some of the pressure from services.
segments.tr: - **Bens.** Os preços de muitos bens manufaturados têm estado mais estáveis, o que ajuda a compensar parte da pressão vinda dos serviços.

segments.src: A core reading of 0.3% suggests that underlying price growth remains steady rather than accelerating.
segments.tr: Uma leitura do núcleo de 0,3% sugere que o crescimento subjacente dos preços permanece estável em vez de acelerar.

segments.src: It also shows that it hasn't cooled as much as policymakers might prefer.
segments.tr: Também mostra que não esfriou tanto quanto os formuladores de políticas gostariam.

segments.src: ## Why One Hot Month Doesn't Settle the Debate
segments.tr: ## Por Que Um Mês Forte Não Define o Debate

segments.tr: É tentador tratar cada relatório mensal como um veredito definitivo.

segments.src: Economists are generally more careful, for several reasons.
segments.tr: Os economistas são geralmente mais cautelosos, por vários motivos.

segments.src: **Monthly data is noisy.** Seasonal adjustments, weather events, and temporary supply disruptions can all distort a single month.
segments.tr: **Os dados mensais têm ruídos.** Ajustes sazonais, eventos climáticos e interrupções temporárias de oferta podem distorcer um único mês.

segments.src: A figure that looks high may be partly reversed the next month.
segments.tr: Um número que parece alto pode ser parcialmente revertido no mês seguinte.

segments.src: **Energy can reverse.** If the increase came from a short-term spike in fuel or utility costs, prices may ease later.
segments.tr: **A energia pode reverter.** Se o aumento veio de um pico de curto prazo nos custos de combustível ou energia, os preços podem diminuir mais tarde.

segments.src: The effect on headline inflation would then fade.
segments.tr: O efeito na inflação cheia iria então desaparecer.

segments.src: **Core is the steadier guide.** Because core inflation strips out the most volatile items, many analysts consider it a better signal of where prices are going over the next several months.
segments.tr: **O núcleo é o guia mais estável.** Como o núcleo da inflação exclui os itens mais voláteis, muitos analistas o consideram um sinal melhor de para onde os preços estão indo nos próximos meses.

segments.src: A steady 0.3% is neither a clear sign of re-acceleration nor of a sustained cooling.
segments.tr: Um 0,3% constante não é um sinal claro de desaceleração sustentada nem de reaceleração.

segments.src: **Trends matter more than points.** Analysts often look at three-month and six-month averages, as well as year-over-year changes, to see through temporary swings.
segments.tr: **Tendências importam mais do que pontos isolados.** Os analistas frequentemente observam as médias de três e seis meses, bem como as variações ano a ano, para enxergar através das oscilações temporárias.

segments.src: One reading above forecasts does not establish a new trend, just as one below forecasts would not have ended the debate.
segments.tr: Uma leitura acima das previsões não estabelece uma nova tendência, assim como uma abaixo das previsões não teria encerrado o debate.

segments.src: **Revisions and surveys can change the picture.** Government statistical agencies sometimes revise earlier figures, and surveys of consumers and businesses offer additional context about price expectations.
segments.tr: **Revisões e pesquisas podem mudar o cenário.** As agências governamentais de estatística às vezes revisam dados anteriores, e pesquisas com consumidores e empresas oferecem contexto adicional sobre as expectativas de preços.

segments.src: ## What It Means for Households
segments.tr: ## O Que Isso Significa para as Famílias

segments.tr: Para a maioria das famílias, o efeito prático de um aumento liderado pela energia aparece no posto de gasolina e nas contas de serviços públicos.

segments.tr: Itulah pola yang terlihat pada bulan Oktober.

segments.src: ## Other Categories in the Mix
segments.tr: ## Kategori Lain dalam Campuran

segments.src: Energy was not the only contributor.
segments.tr: Energi bukan satu-satunya penyumbang.

segments.src: Several other areas typically shape the monthly reading:
segments.tr: Beberapa area lain biasanya membentuk angka bulanan:

segments.src: - **Shelter.** Rent and housing-related costs make up the largest single share of the index. They move slowly, but they rarely fall quickly, so they often hold core inflation up.
segments.tr: - **Papan (Shelter).** Biaya sewa dan terkait perumahan menyusun porsi tunggal terbesar dari indeks. Biaya ini bergerak lambat, tetapi jarang turun dengan cepat, sehingga sering menahan inflasi inti tetap tinggi.

segments.src: - **Food.** Grocery and restaurant prices can add or subtract a few hundredths of a percentage point depending on the month.
segments.tr: - **Makanan.** Harga bahan makanan dan restoran dapat menambah atau mengurangi beberapa perseratus persentase poin tergantung pada bulannya.

segments.src: - **Services.** Items such as medical care, insurance, and transportation services have been persistent sources of upward pressure in recent years.
segments.tr: - **Jasa.** Item seperti perawatan medis, asuransi, dan layanan transportasi telah menjadi sumber tekanan ke atas yang persisten dalam beberapa tahun terakhir.

segments.src: - **Goods.** Prices for many manufactured goods have been flatter, which helps offset some of the pressure from services.
segments.tr: - **Barang.** Harga untuk banyak barang manufaktur cenderung lebih datar, yang membantu mengimbangi sebagian tekanan dari sektor jasa.

segments.src: A core reading of 0.3% suggests that underlying price growth remains steady rather than accelerating.
segments.tr: Angka inti sebesar 0,3% menunjukkan bahwa pertumbuhan harga dasar tetap stabil dan bukannya mempercepat.

segments.src: It also shows that it hasn't cooled as much as policymakers might prefer.
segments.tr: Ini juga menunjukkan bahwa inflasi belum mendingin sebanyak yang diharapkan oleh para pembuat kebijakan.

segments.src: ## Why One Hot Month Doesn't Settle the Debate
segments.tr: ## Mengapa Satu Bulan yang Panas Tidak Mengakhiri Perdebatan

segments.src: It is tempting to treat each monthly report as a verdict.
segments.tr: Sangat menggoda untuk memperlakukan setiap laporan bulanan sebagai keputusan akhir.

segments.src: Economists are generally more careful, for several reasons.
segments.tr: Para ekonom umumnya lebih berhati-hati, karena beberapa alasan.

segments.src: **Monthly data is noisy.** Seasonal adjustments, weather events, and temporary supply disruptions can all distort a single month.
segments.tr: **Data bulanan penuh gangguan (noisy).** Penyesuaian musiman, peristiwa cuaca, dan gangguan pasokan sementara semuanya dapat mendistorsi satu bulan.

segments.src: A figure that looks high may be partly reversed the next month.
segments.tr: Angka yang terlihat tinggi mungkin sebagian akan berbalik pada bulan berikutnya.

segments.src: **Energy can reverse.** If the increase came from a short-term spike in fuel or utility costs, prices may ease later.
segments.tr: **Energi dapat berbalik.** Jika kenaikan berasal dari lonjakan jangka pendek dalam biaya bahan bakar atau utilitas, harga dapat mereda kemudian.

segments.src: The effect on headline inflation would then fade.
segments.tr: Efek pada inflasi utama kemudian akan memudar.

segments.src: **Core is the steadier guide.** Because core inflation strips out the most volatile items, many analysts consider it a better signal of where prices are going over the next several months.
segments.tr: **Inti adalah panduan yang lebih stabil.** Karena inflasi inti menghilangkan item yang paling volatil, banyak analis menganggapnya sebagai sinyal yang lebih baik tentang ke mana arah harga selama beberapa bulan ke depan.

segments.src: A steady 0.3% is neither a clear sign of re-acceleration nor of a sustained cooling.
segments.tr: Angka 0,3% yang stabil bukanlah tanda jelas dari akselerasi ulang maupun pendinginan yang berkelanjutan.

segments.src: **Trends matter more than points.** Analysts often look at three-month and six-month averages, as well as year-over-year changes, to see through temporary swings.
segments.tr: **Tren lebih penting daripada poin data.** Analis sering melihat rata-rata tiga bulan dan enam bulan, serta perubahan tahun-ke-tahun, untuk melihat melampaui fluktuasi sementara.

segments.src: One reading above forecasts does not establish a new trend, just as one below forecasts would not have ended the debate.
segments.tr: Satu data di atas perkiraan tidak membentuk tren baru, sama seperti satu data di bawah perkiraan tidak akan mengakhiri perdebatan.

segments.src: **Revisions and surveys can change the picture.** Government statistical agencies sometimes revise earlier figures, and surveys of consumers and businesses offer additional context about price expectations.
segments.tr: **Revisi dan survei dapat mengubah gambaran.** Lembaga statistik pemerintah terkadang merevisi angka-angka sebelumnya, dan survei konsumen serta bisnis menawarkan konteks tambahan tentang ekspektasi harga.

segments.src: ## What It Means for Households
segments.tr: ## Apa Artiannya bagi Rumah Tangga

segments.src: For most households, the practical effect of an energy-led increase shows up at the gas pump and on utility bills.
segments.tr: Bagi sebagian besar rumah tangga, efek praktis dari kenaikan yang dipicu energi terlihat di pompa bensin dan pada tagihan utilitas.

segments.src: Those costs are hard to avoid, so they can feel larger than the headline number suggests.
segments.tr: Biaya-biaya tersebut sulit dihindari, sehingga terasa lebih besar daripada yang ditunjukkan oleh angka utama.

segments.src: Higher energy costs may also leave less room in budgets for other spending.
segments.tr: Biaya energi yang lebih tinggi juga dapat menyisakan lebih sedikit ruang dalam anggaran untuk pengeluaran lain.

segments.src: Some general points to keep in mind:
segments.tr: Beberapa poin umum yang perlu diingat:

segments.src: - Track your own spending categories rather than relying only on national averages. Your personal inflation rate depends on what you buy.
segments.tr: - Pantau kategori pengeluaran Anda sendiri daripada hanya mengandalkan rata-rata nasional. Tingkat inflasi pribadi Anda tergantung pada apa yang Anda beli.

segments.src: - Seasonal changes in heating and cooling costs can be planned for ahead of time.
segments.tr: - Perubahan musiman dalam biaya pemanas dan pendingin dapat direncanakan terlebih dahulu.

segments.src: - Short-term price moves in energy often don't last, so large financial decisions made on one month's data carry more risk.
segments.tr: - Pergerakan harga jangka pendek pada energi sering kali tidak bertahan lama, sehingga keputusan keuangan besar yang dibuat berdasarkan data satu bulan membawa risiko lebih besar.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Apa yang Perlu Dipantau Selanjutnya

segments.src: Several indicators will help show whether October was a one-off or part of a broader pattern:
segments.tr: Beberapa indikator akan membantu menunjukkan apakah bulan Oktober merupakan kejadian sekali saja atau bagian dari pola yang lebih luas:

segments.src: - **Next month's CPI report**, especially the core figure and the energy component.
segments.tr: - **Laporan IHK bulan depan**, terutama angka inti dan komponen energi.

segments.src: - **Wholesale and producer prices**, which can signal pressure that has not yet reached consumers.
segments.tr: - **Harga grosir dan produsen**, yang dapat memberi sinyal tekanan yang belum mencapai konsumen.

segments.src: - **Wage growth**, since rising pay can sustain demand for services.
segments.tr: - **Pertumbuhan upah**, karena kenaikan gaji dapat mempertahankan permintaan akan layanan/jasa.

segments.src: - **Central bank communications**, which show how policymakers read the data and whether they see risks to their inflation goal.
segments.tr: - **Komunikasi bank sentral**, yang menunjukkan bagaimana para pembuat kebijakan membaca data dan apakah mereka melihat risiko terhadap target inflasi mereka.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## Kesimpulan

segments.src: October's 0.4% increase was a firmer reading than expected, and energy did much of the work.
segments.tr: Kenaikan 0,4% di bulan Oktober adalah angka yang lebih kuat dari yang diperkirakan, dan energi berperan besar di dalamnya.

segments.src: With core inflation steady at 0.3%, the report points to ongoing but not accelerating underlying price pressure.
segments.tr: Dengan inflasi inti yang stabil di angka 0,3%, laporan ini menunjukkan tekanan harga dasar yang masih berlangsung tetapi tidak mempercepat.

segments.src: A single month is a data point, not a trend, and the inflation debate will turn on whether the coming months confirm or reverse what October showed.
segments.tr: Satu bulan adalah satu poin data, bukan tren, dan perdebatan inflasi akan bergantung pada apakah bulan-bulan mendatang mengonfirmasi atau membalikkan apa yang ditunjukkan pada bulan Oktober.

ja.title: エネルギーがインフレを押し上げ：10月消費者物価の0.4%上昇の真相

segments.src: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, a faster pace than most forecasters expected, while core inflation, which leaves out food and energy, held at 0.3%.
segments.tr: 10月の消費者物価指数は0.4%上昇し、多くの予測専門家の予想を上回るペースとなりました。一方、食品とエネルギーを除いたコアインフレ率は0.3%で横ばいでした。

segments.src: The gap between those two numbers points to the main driver of the month: energy.
segments.tr: これら2つの数値の格差は、今月の主な要因がエネルギーであることを示しています。

segments.src: This article explains what the headline and core figures mean, which categories fed the increase, and why one strong monthly reading doesn't settle the debate over where inflation is heading.
segments.tr: この記事では、総合数値とコア数値の意味、上昇を後押ししたカテゴリー、そして1ヶ月の強い結果だけではインフレの今後の動向に関する議論が解決しない理由について説明します。

segments.src: ## The Numbers at a Glance
segments.tr: ## 数値の概要

segments.src: - **Headline consumer prices:** up 0.4% for the month, above forecasts.
segments.tr: - **総合消費者物価：** 前月比0.4%上昇、予想を上回る。

segments.src: - **Core prices (excluding food and energy):** up 0.3%, unchanged from the prior pace.
segments.tr: - **コア物価（食品とエネルギーを除く）：** 0.3%上昇、前回のペースから不変。

segments.src: - **The difference:** roughly 0.1 percentage point, which is attributable mostly to more volatile categories such as energy.
segments.tr: - **差：** 約0.1ポイント。これは主にエネルギーなど価格変動の激しいカテゴリーに起因します。

segments.src: A 0.4% monthly gain looks modest, but economists often look at what it implies over a year.
segments.tr: 月間0.4%の上昇は控えめに見えますが、エコノミストはそれが年間で何を意味するかに注目することがよくあります。

segments.src: If a 0.4% pace held for twelve months, it would compound to close to 5% annual inflation.
segments.tr: 0.4%のペースが12ヶ月間続くと、年率換算で5%近くに達します。

segments.src: That is well above the 2% target the Federal Reserve has set.
segments.tr: これは、連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）が設定した2%の目標を大きく上回っています。

segments.src: A 0.3% pace compounds to a little under 4%.
segments.tr: 0.3%のペースを年率換算すると4%を少し下回る程度です。

segments.src: That is why even small monthly differences get close attention.
segments.tr: そのため、月間のわずかな違いであっても細心の注意が払われます。

segments.src: ## Why Energy Mattered So Much
segments.tr: ## なぜエネルギーがこれほど重要だったのか

segments.src: Energy prices are among the most volatile parts of the consumer price index.
segments.tr: エネルギー価格は、消費者物価指数の中で最も変動が激しい部分の1つです。

segments.src: Gasoline, electricity, and natural gas can all move sharply from month to month because of weather, refinery activity, seasonal demand, and global supply conditions.
segments.tr: ガソリン、電気、天然ガスはすべて、天候、製油所の稼働状況、季節的需要、世界的な供給状況によって、月ごとに大きく変動する可能性があります。

segments.src: Energy has an outsized effect on headline readings for three reasons:
segments.tr: エネルギーが総合数値に極めて大きな影響を与えるのには、3つの理由があります。

segments.src: 1. **It is bought often.** Households fill up their tanks and pay utility bills every month, so changes are felt quickly.
segments.tr: 1. **購入頻度が高いこと。** 家計は毎月ガソリンを給油し、光熱費を支払うため、変化をすぐに実感します。

segments.src: 2. **It is volatile.** A swing of several percent in a single month is not unusual, which can move the overall index even when other prices are steady.
segments.tr: 2. **変動が大きいこと。** 単一の月で数パーセントの変動は珍しくなく、他の価格が安定していても指数全体を動かす可能性があります。

segments.src: 3. **It feeds into other costs.** Higher fuel and power costs can eventually show up in transportation, shipping, and food prices.
segments.tr: 3. **他のコストに波及すること。** 燃料費や電力コストの上昇は、最終的に輸送費、出荷費、食品価格に跳ね返る可能性があります。

segments.src: Because the headline index includes energy and the core index does not, an energy-led month tends to lift the first number while leaving the second largely unchanged.
segments.tr: 総合指数にはエネルギーが含まれ、コア指数には含まれないため、エネルギー主導の月は前者の数値の押し上げにつながる一方で、後者の数値はほとんど変化しない傾向があります。

segments.src: That is the pattern seen in October.
segments.tr: これが10月に見られたパターンです。

segments.src: ## Other Categories in the Mix
segments.tr: ## 内訳に含まれるその他のカテゴリー

segments.src: Energy was not the only contributor.
segments.tr: 要因はエネルギーだけではありませんでした。

segments.src: Several other areas typically shape the monthly reading:
segments.tr: 通常、他のいくつかの分野も月間の数値を形成します。

segments.src: - **Shelter.** Rent and housing-related costs make up the largest single share of the index. They move slowly, but they rarely fall quickly, so they often hold core inflation up.
segments.tr: - **住居費。** 家賃や住宅関連コストは、指数の中で最大のシェアを占めます。動きは緩やかですが、急速に下がることはめったにないため、コアインフレ率を維持する要因となることがよくあります。

segments.src: - **Food.** Grocery and restaurant prices can add or subtract a few hundredths of a percentage point depending on the month.
segments.tr: - **食品。** 食料品やレストランの価格は、月によって数十パーセントポイントを加算または減算する可能性があります。

segments.src: - **Services.** Items such as medical care, insurance, and transportation services have been persistent sources of upward pressure in recent years.
segments.tr: - **サービス。** 医療、保険、輸送サービスなどの項目は、近年、上昇圧力の持続的な源となっています。

segments.src: - **Goods.** Prices for many manufactured goods have been flatter, which helps offset some of the pressure from services.
segments.tr: - **財（商品）。** 多くの工業製品の価格はより横ばい傾向にあり、サービスからの圧力の一部を相殺するのに役立っています。

segments.src: A core reading of 0.3% suggests that underlying price growth remains steady rather than accelerating.
segments.tr: コア数値の0.3%は、基調的な物価上昇が加速しているのではなく、安定していることを示唆しています。

segments.src: It also shows that it hasn't cooled as much as policymakers might prefer.
segments.tr: また、政策立案者が望むほどには減速していないことも示しています。

segments.src: ## Why One Hot Month Doesn't Settle the Debate
segments.tr: ## 1ヶ月の強い結果だけでは議論が解決しない理由

segments.src: It is tempting to treat each monthly report as a verdict.
segments.tr: 毎月のレポートを決定的な判断として扱いたくなるものです。

segments.src: Economists are generally more careful, for several reasons.
segments.tr: しかし、エコノミストはいくつかの理由から、一般的により慎重です。

segments.src: **Monthly data is noisy.** Seasonal adjustments, weather events, and temporary supply disruptions can all distort a single month.
segments.tr: **月次データにはノイズが含まれます。** 季節調整、天候イベント、一時的な供給の混乱はすべて、単一の月を歪める可能性があります。

segments.src: A figure that looks high may be partly reversed the next month.
segments.tr: 高く見える数値でも、翌月には一部が押し戻される（反転する）ことがあります。

segments.src: **Energy can reverse.** If the increase came from a short-term spike in fuel or utility costs, prices may ease later.
segments.tr: **エネルギーは反転することがあります。** 上昇が燃料費や光熱費の一時的な急騰によるものである場合、価格は後で和らぐ可能性があります。

segments.src: The effect on headline inflation would then fade.
segments.tr: その場合、総合インフレへの影響は薄れることになります。

segments.src: **Core is the steadier guide.** Because core inflation strips out the most volatile items, many analysts consider it a better signal of where prices are going over the next several months.
segments.tr: **コア指標の方がより安定した目安になります。** コアインフレ率は最も変動の激しい項目を除外しているため、多くのアナリストは今後数ヶ月間の物価の動向を示すより良いシグナルだと考えています。

segments.src: A steady 0.3% is neither a clear sign of re-acceleration nor of a sustained cooling.
segments.tr: 安定した0.3%は、明確な再加速の兆候でも、持続的な鈍化の兆候でもありません。

segments.src: **Trends matter more than points.** Analysts often look at three-month and six-month averages, as well as year-over-year changes, to see through temporary swings.
segments.tr: **単一の数値よりもトレンドが重要です。** アナリストは、一時的な変動を見極めるために、前年比の変化だけでなく、3ヶ月平均や6ヶ月平均に注目することがよくあります。

segments.src: One reading above forecasts does not establish a new trend, just as one below forecasts would not have ended the debate.
segments.tr: 予想を下回る数値が1つあっても議論が終わらないのと同様に、予想を上回る数値が1つ出たからといって新しいトレンドが確立されるわけではありません。

segments.src: **Revisions and surveys can change the picture.** Government statistical agencies sometimes revise earlier figures, and surveys of consumers and businesses offer additional context about price expectations.
segments.tr: **改定値や調査によって状況が変わる可能性があります。** 政府の統計機関が以前の数字を改定することがあり、消費者や企業の調査により、物価予想に関するさらなる背景が提供されます。

segments.src: ## What It Means for Households
segments.tr: ## 家計にとっての意味

segments.src: For most households, the practical effect of an energy-led increase shows up at the gas pump and on utility bills.
segments.tr: 大部分の家計にとって、エネルギー主導の上昇の実際の影響は、ガソリンスタンドや光熱費の請求書に現れます。

segments.src: Those costs are hard to avoid, so they can feel larger than the headline number suggests.
segments.tr: これらのコストは回避するのが難しいため、総合数値が示す以上に大きく感じられることがあります。

segments.src: Higher energy costs may also leave less room in budgets for other spending.
segments.tr: エネルギーコストの上昇は、家計における他の支出の余裕を奪う可能性もあります。

segments.src: Some general points to keep in mind:
segments.tr: 覚えておくべき一般的なポイント：

segments.src: - Track your own spending categories rather than relying only on national averages. Your personal inflation rate depends on what you buy.
segments.tr: - 全国平均だけに頼るのではなく、ご自身の支出カテゴリーを把握しましょう。個人のインフレ率は購入するものによって異なります。

segments.src: - Seasonal changes in heating and cooling costs can be planned for ahead of time.
segments.tr: - 暖房費や冷房費の季節的な変動は、あらかじめ計画を立てておくことができます。

segments.src: - Short-term price moves in energy often don't last, so large financial decisions made on one month's data carry more risk.
segments.tr: - エネルギーの短期的価格変動は長続きしないことが多いため、1ヶ月のデータに基づいて大きな財務上の決定を下すことには、より大きなリスクが伴います。

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## 次に注目すべきポイント

segments.src: Several indicators will help show whether October was a one-off or part of a broader pattern:
segments.tr: 10月の結果が一過性のものか、それともより広範なパターンの一部であるかを見極めるのに、いくつかの指標が役立ちます。

segments.src: - **Next month's CPI report**, especially the core figure and the energy component.
segments.tr: - **来月のCPIレポート**、特にコア数値とエネルギー構成要素。

segments.src: - **Wholesale and producer prices**, which can signal pressure that has not yet reached consumers.
segments.tr: - **卸売・生産者物価**。これは、まだ消費者に達していない圧力を示す可能性があります。

segments.src: - **Wage growth**, since rising pay can sustain demand for services.
segments.tr: - **賃金の伸び**。賃金の上昇はサービスへの需要を維持させる可能性があるためです。

segments.src: - **Central bank communications**, which show how policymakers read the data and whether they see risks to their inflation goal.
segments.tr: - **中央銀行の発言**。政策立案者がデータをどのように読み解き、インフレ目標に対するリスクを見ているかを示します。

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## 結論

segments.src: October's 0.4% increase was a firmer reading than expected, and energy did much of the work.
segments.tr: 10月の0.4%の上昇は予想よりも堅調な数値であり、エネルギーが大きな役割を果たしました。

segments.src: With core inflation steady at 0.3%, the report points to ongoing but not accelerating underlying price pressure.
segments.tr: コアインフレ率が0.3%で横ばいであることから、このレポートは基調的な物価圧力が加速はしていないものの継続していることを示しています。

segments.src: A single month is a data point, not a trend, and the inflation debate will turn on whether the coming months confirm or reverse what October showed.
segments.tr: 1ヶ月のデータは単なるデータポイントの1つであり、トレンドではありません。インフレに関する議論は、今後数ヶ月が10月の示された傾向を裏付けるか反転させるかにかかっています。

de.title: Energie treibt die Inflation nach oben: Hintergründe zum Anstieg der Verbraucherpreise im Oktober um 0,4 %

segments.src: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, a faster pace than most forecasters expected, while core inflation, which leaves out food and energy, held at 0.3%.
segments.tr: Die Verbraucherpreise stiegen im Oktober um 0,4 %, was ein schnelleres Tempo darstellt als von den meisten Prognostikern erwartet, während die Kerninflation, bei der Lebensmittel und Energie unberücksichtigt bleiben, bei 0,3 % verharrte.

segments.src: The gap between those two numbers points to the main driver of the month: energy.
segments.tr: Die Lücke zwischen diesen beiden Zahlen verweist auf den Haupttreiber des Monats: Energie.

segments.src: This article explains what the headline and core figures mean, which categories fed the increase, and why one strong monthly reading doesn't settle the debate over where inflation is heading.
segments.tr: Dieser Artikel erklärt, was die Gesamt- und Kernzahlen bedeuten, welche Kategorien den Anstieg speisten und warum ein starker Monatsmesswert die Debatte darüber, wohin sich die Inflation bewegt, nicht entscheidet.

segments.src: ## The Numbers at a Glance
segments.tr: ## Die Zahlen auf einen Blick

segments.src: - **Headline consumer prices:** up 0.4% for the month, above forecasts.
segments.tr: - **Gesamt-Verbraucherpreise:** im Laufe des Monats um 0,4 % gestiegen, über den Prognosen.

segments.src: - **Core prices (excluding food and energy):** up 0.3%, unchanged from the prior pace.
segments.tr: - **Kernpreise (ohne Lebensmittel und Energie):** um 0,3 % gestiegen, unverändert gegenüber dem Vormonat.

segments.src: - **The difference:** roughly 0.1 percentage point, which is attributable mostly to more volatile categories such as energy.
segments.tr: - **Der Unterschied:** grob 0,1 Prozentpunkte, was hauptsächlich volatileren Kategorien wie Energie zuschreibbar ist.

segments.src: A 0.4% monthly gain looks modest, but economists often look at what it implies over a year.
segments.tr: Ein monatlicher Zuwachs von 0,4 % wirkt bescheiden, aber Ökonomen betrachten oft, was dies über ein Jahr hinweg bedeutet.

segments.src: If a 0.4% pace held for twelve months, it would compound to close to 5% annual inflation.
segments.tr: Würde ein Tempo von 0,4 % zwölf Monate lang anhalten, würde dies auf eine jährliche Inflation von nahe 5 % hinauslaufen.

segments.src: That is well above the 2% target the Federal Reserve has set.
segments.tr: Das liegt deutlich über dem von der Federal Reserve festgelegten Ziel von 2 %.

segments.src: A 0.3% pace compounds to a little under 4%.
segments.tr: Ein Tempo von 0,3 % summiert sich auf knapp unter 4 %.

segments.src: That is why even small monthly differences get close attention.
segments.tr: Aus diesem Grund erhalten selbst kleine monatliche Differenzen große Aufmerksamkeit.

segments.src: ## Why Energy Mattered So Much
segments.tr: ## Warum Energie so wichtig war

segments.src: Energy prices are among the most volatile parts of the consumer price index.
segments.tr: Energiepreise gehören zu den volatilsten Teilen des Verbraucherpreisindex.

segments.src: Gasoline, electricity, and natural gas can all move sharply from month to month because of weather, refinery activity, seasonal demand, and global supply conditions.
segments.tr: Benzin, Strom und Erdgas können sich aufgrund von Wetter, Raffinerieaktivität, saisonaler Nachfrage und globalen Angebotsbedingungen von Monat zu Monat stark verändern.

segments.src: Energy has an outsized effect on headline readings for three reasons:
segments.tr: Energie hat aus drei Gründen einen übergroßen Effekt auf die Gesamtwerte:

segments.src: 1. **It is bought often.** Households fill up their tanks and pay utility bills every month, so changes are felt quickly.
segments.tr: 1. **Sie wird oft gekauft.** Haushalte füllen jeden Monat ihre Tanks und bezahlen Energierechnungen, sodass Veränderungen schnell spürbar sind.

segments.src: 2. **It is volatile.** A swing of several percent in a single month is not unusual, which can move the overall index even when other prices are steady.
segments.tr: 2. **Sie ist volatil.** Ein Ausschlag von mehreren Prozent in einem einzigen Monat ist keine Seltenheit, was den Gesamtindex bewegen kann, selbst wenn andere Preise stabil bleiben.

segments.src: 3. **It feeds into other costs.** Higher fuel and power costs can eventually show up in transportation, shipping, and food prices.
segments.tr: 3. **Sie fließt in andere Kosten ein.** Höhere Treibstoff- und Energiekosten können schließlich in Transport-, Fracht- und Lebensmittelpreise einfließen.

segments.src: Because the headline index includes energy and the core index does not, an energy-led month tends to lift the first number while leaving the second largely unchanged.
segments.tr: Da der Gesamtindex Energie enthält und der Kernindex nicht, neigt ein von Energie geführter Monat dazu, die erste Zahl nach oben zu ziehen, während die zweite weitgehend unverändert bleibt.

segments.src: That is the pattern seen in October.
segments.tr: Das ist das im Oktober beobachtete Muster.

segments.src: ## Other Categories in the Mix
segments.tr: ## Andere Kategorien im Mix

segments.src: Energy was not the only contributor.
segments.tr: Energie war nicht der einzige Mitwirkende.

segments.src: Several other areas typically shape the monthly reading:
segments.tr: Mehrere andere Bereiche prägen typischerweise den Monatsmesswert:

segments.src: - **Shelter.** Rent and housing-related costs make up the largest single share of the index. They move slowly, but they rarely fall quickly, so they often hold core inflation up.
segments.tr: - **Mieten und Wohnen.** Miete und wohnungsbezogene Kosten machen den größten Einzelanteil des Index aus. Sie bewegen sich langsam, aber sie fallen selten schnell, weshalb sie die Kerninflation oft hochhalten.

segments.src: - **Food.** Grocery and restaurant prices can add or subtract a few hundredths of a percentage point depending on the month.
segments.tr: - **Lebensmittel.** Lebensmittel- und Restaurantpreise können je nach Monat einige Hundertstel eines Prozentpunkts hinzufügen oder abziehen.

segments.src: - **Services.** Items such as medical care, insurance, and transportation services have been persistent sources of upward pressure in recent years.
segments.tr: - **Dienstleistungen.** Posten wie medizinische Versorgung, Versicherungen und Transportdienstleistungen waren in den letzten Jahren anhaltende Quellen von Aufwärtsdruck.

segments.src: - **Goods.** Prices for many manufactured goods have been flatter, which helps offset some of the pressure from services.
segments.tr: - **Güter.** Die Preise für viele hergestellte Waren waren flacher, was hilft, einen Teil des Drucks von Dienstleistungen auszugleichen.

segments.src: A core reading of 0.3% suggests that underlying price growth remains steady rather than accelerating.
segments.tr: Ein Kernwert von 0,3 % legt nahe, dass das zugrundeliegende Preiswachstum stabil bleibt, anstatt sich zu beschleunigen.

segments.src: It also shows that it hasn't cooled as much as policymakers might prefer.
segments.tr: Es zeigt auch, dass es sich nicht so stark abgekühlt hat, wie es politische Entscheidungsträger bevorzugen könnten.

segments.src: ## Why One Hot Month Doesn't Settle the Debate
segments.tr: ## Warum ein heißer Monat die Debatte nicht entscheidet

segments.src: It is tempting to treat each monthly report as a verdict.
segments.tr: Es ist verlockend, jeden Monatsbericht als Urteil zu behandeln.

segments.src: Economists are generally more careful, for several reasons.
segments.tr: Ökonomen sind im Allgemeinen vorsichtiger, aus mehreren Gründen.

segments.src: **Monthly data is noisy.** Seasonal adjustments, weather events, and temporary supply disruptions can all distort a single month.
segments.tr: **Monatliche Daten sind verrauscht.** Saisonale Anpassungen, Wetterereignisse und temporäre Lieferunterbrechungen können einen einzelnen Monat verzerren.

segments.src: A figure that looks high may be partly reversed the next month.
segments.tr: Ein Wert, der hoch erscheint, kann im nächsten Monat teilweise umgekehrt werden.

segments.src: **Energy can reverse.** If the increase came from a short-term spike in fuel or utility costs, prices may ease later.
segments.tr: **Energie kann sich umkehren.** Wenn der Anstieg von einem kurzfristigen Spike bei Treibstoff- oder Energiekosten kam, könnten sich die Preise später wieder entspannen.

segments.src: The effect on headline inflation would then fade.
segments.tr: Der Effekt auf die Gesamtinflation würde dann abklingen.

segments.src: **Core is the steadier guide.** Because core inflation strips out the most volatile items, many analysts consider it a better signal of where prices are going over the next several months.
segments.tr: **Der Kern ist der stabilere Leitfaden.** Da die Kerninflation die volatilsten Posten herausrechnet, betrachten viele Analysten sie als besseres Signal dafür, wohin sich die Preise in den nächsten Monaten bewegen.

segments.src: A steady 0.3% is neither a clear sign of re-acceleration nor of a sustained cooling.
segments.tr: Ein stabiler Wert von 0,3 % ist weder ein klares Zeichen einer Wiederbeschleunigung noch einer nachhaltigen Abkühlung.

segments.src: **Trends matter more than points.** Analysts often look at three-month and six-month averages, as well as year-over-year changes, to see through temporary swings.
segments.tr: **Trends zählen mehr als Punkte.** Analysten betrachten oft Drei- und Sechsmonatsdurchschnitte sowie Veränderungen im Jahresvergleich, um durch temporäre Schwankungen hindurchzusehen.

segments.src: One reading above forecasts does not establish a new trend, just as one below forecasts would not have ended the debate.
segments.tr: Ein Messwert über den Prognosen begründet keinen neuen Trend, genauso wenig wie ein Wert unter den Prognosen die Debatte beendet hätte.

segments.src: **Revisions and surveys can change the picture.** Government statistical agencies sometimes revise earlier figures, and surveys of consumers and businesses offer additional context about price expectations.
segments.tr: **Revisionen und Umfragen können das Bild verändern.** Staatliche Statistikbehörden revidieren manchmal frühere Zahlen, und Umfragen unter Verbrauchern und Unternehmen bieten zusätzlichen Kontext zu Preiserwartungen.

segments.src: ## What It Means for Households
segments.tr: ## Was es für Haushalte bedeutet

segments.src: For most households, the practical effect of an energy-led increase shows up at the gas pump and on utility bills.
segments.tr: Für die meisten Haushalte zeigt sich der praktische Effekt eines von Energie getriebenen Anstiegs an der Zapfsäule und auf Energierechnungen.

segments.src: Those costs are hard to avoid, so they can feel larger than the headline number suggests.
segments.tr: Diese Kosten sind schwer zu vermeiden, sodass sie größer wirken können, als die Gesamtzahl nahelegt.

segments.src: Higher energy costs may also leave less room in budgets for other spending.
segments.tr: Höhere Energiekosten lassen möglicherweise auch weniger Spielraum im Budget für andere Ausgaben.

segments.src: Some general points to keep in mind:
segments.tr: Einige allgemeine Punkte, die man im Hinterkopf behalten sollte:

segments.src: - Track your own spending categories rather than relying only on national averages. Your personal inflation rate depends on what you buy.
segments.tr: - Verfolgen Sie Ihre eigenen Ausgabenkategorien anstatt sich nur auf nationale Durchschnitte zu verlassen. Ihre persönliche Inflationsrate hängt davon ab, was Sie kaufen.

segments.src: - Seasonal changes in heating and cooling costs can be planned for ahead of time.
segments.tr: - Saisonale Änderungen bei Heiz- und Kühlkosten können im Voraus eingeplant werden.

segments.src: - Short-term price moves in energy often don't last, so large financial decisions made on one month's data carry more risk.
segments.tr: - Kurzfristige Preisbewegungen bei Energie halten oft nicht an, sodass große finanzielle Entscheidungen, die auf den Daten eines Monats basieren, ein höheres Risiko bergen.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Worauf als Nächstes zu achten ist

segments.src: Several indicators will help show whether October was a one-off or part of a broader pattern:
segments.tr: Mehrere Indikatoren werden helfen zu zeigen, ob der Oktober ein Einzelfall oder Teil eines breiteren Musters war:

segments.src: - **Next month's CPI report**, especially the core figure and the energy component.
segments.tr: - **Der Verbraucherpreisbericht des nächsten Monats**, insbesondere die Kernzahl und die Energiekomponente.

segments.src: - **Wholesale and producer prices**, which can signal pressure that has not yet reached consumers.
segments.tr: - **Großhandels- und Erzeugerpreise**, die Druck signalisieren können, der die Verbraucher noch nicht erreicht hat.

segments.src: - **Wage growth**, since rising pay can sustain demand for services.
segments.tr: - **Lohnwachstum**, da steigende Bezahlung die Nachfrage nach Dienstleistungen stützen kann.

segments.src: - **Central bank communications**, which show how policymakers read the data and whether they see risks to their inflation goal.
segments.tr: - **Kommunikation der Zentralbank**, die zeigt, wie politische Entscheidungsträger die Daten lesen und ob sie Risiken für ihr Inflationsziel sehen.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## Das Fazit

segments.src: October's 0.4% increase was a firmer reading than expected, and energy did much of the work.
segments.tr: Der Anstieg im Oktober um 0,4 % war ein festerer Messwert als erwartet, und Energie hat viel von der Arbeit geleistet.

segments.src: With core inflation steady at 0.3%, the report points to ongoing but not accelerating underlying price pressure.
segments.tr: Da die Kerninflation stabil bei 0,3 % liegt, verweist der Bericht auf anhaltenden, aber nicht beschleunigten zugrundeliegenden Preisdruck.

segments.src: A single month is a data point, not a trend, and the inflation debate will turn on whether the coming months confirm or reverse what October showed.
segments.tr: Ein einzelner Monat ist ein Datenpunkt, kein Trend, und die Inflationsdebatte wird sich darum drehen, ob die kommenden Monate das bestätigen oder umkehren, was der Oktober gezeigt hat.

segments.tr: Một con số trông có vẻ cao có thể được đảo ngược một phần vào tháng sau.

segments.src: **Energy can reverse.** If the increase came from a short-term spike in fuel or utility costs, prices may ease later.
segments.tr: **Năng lượng có thể đảo ngược.** Nếu sự gia tăng đến từ việc tăng đột biến trong ngắn hạn về chi phí nhiên liệu hoặc tiện ích, giá có thể dịu lại sau đó.

segments.src: The effect on headline inflation would then fade.
segments.tr: Tác động lên lạm phát tổng thể sau đó sẽ mờ dần.

segments.src: **Core is the steadier guide.** Because core inflation strips out the most volatile items, many analysts consider it a better signal of where prices are going over the next several months.
segments.tr: **Lõi là hướng dẫn ổn định hơn.** Vì lạm phát lõi loại bỏ các mặt hàng biến động mạnh nhất, nhiều nhà phân tích coi đó là tín hiệu tốt hơn về việc giá sẽ đi đâu trong vài tháng tới.

segments.src: A steady 0.3% is neither a clear sign of re-acceleration nor of a sustained cooling.
segments.tr: Mức 0,3% ổn định không phải là dấu hiệu rõ ràng về việc tăng tốc trở lại cũng như không phải là sự hạ nhiệt bền vững.

segments.src: **Trends matter more than points.** Analysts often look at three-month and six-month averages, as well as year-over-year changes, to see through temporary swings.
segments.tr: **Xu hướng quan trọng hơn các điểm số.** Các nhà phân tích thường xem xét mức trung bình ba tháng và sáu tháng, cũng như các thay đổi theo năm, để nhìn thấu qua những biến động tạm thời.

segments.src: One reading above forecasts does not establish a new trend, just as one below forecasts would not have ended the debate.
segments.tr: Một chỉ số vượt dự báo không thiết lập một xu hướng mới, cũng như một chỉ số dưới dự báo sẽ không kết thúc cuộc tranh cãi.

segments.src: **Revisions and surveys can change the picture.** Government statistical agencies sometimes revise earlier figures, and surveys of consumers and businesses offer additional context about price expectations.
segments.tr: **Các bản sửa đổi và khảo sát có thể thay đổi bức tranh.** Các cơ quan thống kê chính phủ đôi khi sửa đổi các số liệu trước đó, và các cuộc khảo sát người tiêu dùng và doanh nghiệp cung cấp bối cảnh bổ sung về kỳ vọng giá cả.

segments.src: ## What It Means for Households
segments.tr: **Ý nghĩa đối với các hộ gia đình

segments.src: For most households, the practical effect of an energy-led increase shows up at the gas pump and on utility bills.
segments.tr: Đối với hầu hết các hộ gia đình, tác động thực tế của việc tăng do năng lượng xuất hiện tại trạm xăng và trên hóa đơn tiện ích.

segments.src: Those costs are hard to avoid, so they can feel larger than the headline number suggests.
segments.tr: Những chi phí đó rất khó tránh, vì vậy chúng có thể cảm thấy lớn hơn con số tổng thể gợi ý.

segments.src: Higher energy costs may also leave less room in budgets for other spending.
segments.tr: Chi phí năng lượng cao hơn cũng có thể để lại ít chỗ trống hơn trong ngân sách cho các khoản chi tiêu khác.

segments.src: Some general points to keep in mind:
segments.tr: Một số điểm chung cần ghi nhớ:

segments.src: - Track your own spending categories rather than relying only on national averages. Your personal inflation rate depends on what you buy.
segments.tr: - Theo dõi các danh mục chi tiêu của riêng bạn thay vì chỉ dựa vào mức trung bình quốc gia. Tỷ lệ lạm phát cá nhân của bạn phụ thuộc vào những gì bạn mua.

segments.src: - Seasonal changes in heating and cooling costs can be planned for ahead of time.
segments.tr: - Các thay đổi theo mùa trong chi phí sưởi ấm và làm mát có thể được lên kế hoạch trước.

segments.src: - Short-term price moves in energy often don't last, so large financial decisions made on one month's data carry more risk.
segments.tr: - Biến động giá ngắn hạn về năng lượng thường không kéo dài, vì vậy các quyết định tài chính lớn được thực hiện dựa trên dữ liệu của một tháng mang lại nhiều rủi ro hơn.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Những gì cần theo dõi tiếp theo

segments.src: Several indicators will help show whether October was a one-off or part of a broader pattern:
segments.tr: Một số chỉ báo sẽ giúp cho thấy liệu tháng 10 có phải là một sự kiện một lần hay một phần của mô hình rộng hơn:

segments.src: - **Next month's CPI report**, especially the core figure and the energy component.
segments.tr: - **Báo cáo CPI của tháng tới**, đặc biệt là con số cốt lõi và thành phần năng lượng.

segments.src: - **Wholesale and producer prices**, which can signal pressure that has not yet reached consumers.
segments.tr: - **Giá bán buôn và giá sản xuất**, có thể báo hiệu áp lực chưa đến tay người tiêu dùng.

segments.src: - **Wage growth**, since rising pay can sustain demand for services.
segments.tr: - **Tăng trưởng tiền lương**, vì thu nhập tăng có thể duy trì nhu cầu về dịch vụ.

segments.src: - **Central bank communications**, which show how policymakers read the data and whether they see risks to their inflation goal.
segments.tr: - **Truyền thông của ngân hàng trung ương**, cho thấy cách các nhà hoạch định chính sách đọc dữ liệu và liệu họ có thấy rủi ro đối với mục tiêu lạm phát của mình hay không.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## Điểm mấu chốt

segments.src: October's 0.4% increase was a firmer reading than expected, and energy did much of the work.
segments.tr: Mức tăng 0,4% trong tháng 10 là một con số vững chắc hơn dự kiến, và năng lượng đã làm phần lớn công việc.

segments.src: With core inflation steady at 0.3%, the report points to ongoing but not accelerating underlying price pressure.
segments.tr: Với lạm phát lõi ổn định ở mức 0,3%, báo cáo chỉ ra áp lực giá cơ bản đang tiếp tục nhưng không tăng tốc.

segments.src: A single month is a data point, not a trend, and the inflation debate will turn on whether the coming months confirm or reverse what October showed.
segments.tr: Một tháng duy nhất là một điểm dữ liệu, không phải là một xu hướng, và cuộc tranh cãi về lạm phát sẽ xoay quanh việc liệu những tháng tới có xác nhận hay đảo ngược những gì tháng 10 đã thể hiện hay không.
